summary: Rena Aronovna Aulova was an indologist and linguist who studied at the National University of Uzbekistan from circa 1944 to 1949 and served there as a docent in 1979.

Renate Syed is an indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1974–1982) under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She was attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Renato Dávalos is an indologist and philosopher who studied at UAM, UNAM, El Colegio de México, and the University of Cologne (Ph.D. 2023). From 2023 to 2026, he held a researcher fellow post at the CNRS.
Renjo Akamatsu was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū. He held a post at Ryukoku University from circa 1900 to 1903.
Renshan Yang was a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Jinling Scriptural Press, the Jetavana Hermitage, and the Buddhist Research Society, serving as head of the latter in 1910.
René Daumal worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He pursued his education at Lycée Henri-IV from circa 1925 to 1927 and at the Sorbonne from circa 1927 to 1929.

René Fohalle was a linguist and indologist who studied at the University of Liège, and in Paris under Antoine Meillet and Émile Benveniste. From 1929 to 1969, he served as ordinary professor at the University of Liège.
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki circa 1970–1975, where he later became an emeritus professor in 2016.

René Grousset was a historian, sinologist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Montpellier, he directed the Musée Cernuschi (1933), was conservateur-en-chef at the Guimet Museum (1945), and became an Académie Française member in 1946.

René Guénon was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour, École Polytechnique, the University of Paris, and the Sorbonne, where he studied under Sylvain Lévi circa 1915–1921.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Indology. Educated at Charles University, Humboldt University, SOAS, LSE, and the University of Vienna, where he completed his doctorate and habilitation, he later served as Privatdozent at Vienna and at Weltmuseum Wien.

Reo Fortune was a scholar who studied at Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Cambridge under Thomas Callan Hodson. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1947 to 1971.

Reuben Burrow was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich (~1770–1772) and the Tower of London (~1772–1775), and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1784–1792).

Reuven Kahane was a scholar of Indology and sociology who completed his Ph.D. at UC Berkeley under Neil Smelser (~1966–1970). He served as lecturer and later Professor of Sociology and Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1969–1999).

Revilo Pendleton Oliver was a scholar of classics and Indology who studied at Pomona College and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under William Abbott Oldfather. He served as professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign from 1945 until 1977.
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi was an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University circa 1960–1965 and later served there as Head of Sahityavidya from circa 1977 to 1995.

Rewata Dhamma was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his undergraduate and postgraduate education, including a PhD, at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1956–1967) and also earned a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University (1956–1967).

Ria Kloppenborg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. She studied at Leiden University and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda, and held posts at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University, becoming Professor of History of Religions in 1988.

Richa Negi is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. She earned an M. Tech from Kurukshetra University and a Ph.D. from MNNIT Allahabad, later serving as Head of Department at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
